title: semi-PD: Towards Efficient LLM Serving via Phase-Wise Disaggregated Computation and Unified Storage
technique: SM-level phase-wise disaggregated computation (prefill/decode workers on same GPU, partitioned SM ratio) with unified weight/KV storage and SLO-aware dynamic SM partitioning

optimized_metrics.evidence: we further design a service-level objective (SLO) aware dynamic partitioning algorithm to optimize the SLO attainment
adhering to the TTFT and TPOT constraints, how to schedule the prefill and decode phase of each request to maximize the system throughput is very important
Constraining TTFT and TPOT, as the two components of the service-level objective (SLO), are both essential for user experience

headline_claim.text: semi-PD maintains lower latency at higher request rates, reducing the average end-to-end latency per request by 1.27-2.58× on DeepSeek series models, and serves 1.55-1.72× more requests adhering to latency constraints on Llama series models

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) is the duration between the arrival time and the time when the prefill phase finishes of a request.
metric_definitions.notes: includes queueing/waiting; latency model: 'The TTFT of a single request consists of two parts of latency, i.e., waiting latency, and prefill latency.' (§5)

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Time-per-Output-Token (TPOT) is the average duration to generate the subsequent tokens (except for the first one) of a request. Some works [19] use Time-between-Tokens (TBT) to measure the latency between successive tokens. In this work, we use the TPOT metric.
metric_definitions.notes: TPOT model excludes decode waiting latency: 'we assume the requests are immediately batched for running upon arrival at the decode worker, hence excluding the waiting latency from TPOT'; KV transfer time counted in TPOT in disaggregated systems (§1)

metric_definitions.definition_quote: the agreement between service providers and users determines SLOs (e.g., TTFT ≤ 500ms, TPOT ≤ 100ms) as the latency constraints. To address the importance of SLOs, many works consider serving more requests while adhering to the SLOs, which is also the objective of this work.
serves 1.55-1.72× more requests ... while staying within latency constraints for > 90% of requests
metric_definitions.notes: max request rate sustaining >90% SLO attainment; the word goodput is not used in this form

slo_spec: TTFT and TPOT thresholds per model/dataset (Table 2), e.g. Llama3-8B ShareGPT tight/loose 0.3s/0.15s and 0.4s/0.2s; Llama3-70B 0.85s/0.3s and 1.1s/0.4s; LongBench 2.25s/0.13s,3.0s/0.18s (8B) and 6.0s/0.3s,8.0s/0.4s (70B). Set as 'approximates of 7.5× and 10× of the single request latency as the tight and loose SLOs'. Attainment target >90% (pSLO in Alg. 1).
tradeoff_acknowledged: Analyses TTFT-vs-TPOT interference in unified systems and storage inefficiency (3x higher TPOT from storage shortage) in disaggregated; no explicit cost of semi-PD
models: Llama3-8B, Llama3-70B, Llama3.1-405B, DeepSeek-V2-Lite, DeepSeek-V3 series
workloads: ShareGPT, LongBench, MATH-500, synthetic 95% ShareGPT + 5% long
extractor_notes: Headline mixes mean E2E (DeepSeek) with SLO-constrained request rate (Llama). Instance-scale latency curves use P90 (P99 as secondary), SLO attainment target is >90%. Never uses the word goodput for its metric. SLO thresholds derived as multiples of single-request latency.
